title: Testcontainers 'Could not find a valid Docker environment' after upgrading to Docker Engine 29

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue/PR; short error excerpt quoted.

symptom: After upgrading Docker Engine to 29.0.0 every Testcontainers-based test fails with IllegalStateException "Could not find a valid Docker environment. Please see logs and check configuration". The same setup works on Docker Engine 28.5.2.
cause: Docker Engine 29 raised the minimum client API version it accepts to 1.44. Testcontainers 2.0.1 (docker-java) uses an older fixed API version when none is configured, so the daemon rejects the requests of every client provider strategy and Testcontainers reports that no valid environment was found.
fixSummary: Upgrade Testcontainers to 2.0.2 or newer, which raises the default API version to 1.44. If that is not possible, set the docker-java api.version to 1.44 or higher via ~/.docker-java.properties, a docker-java.properties on the classpath, or a system property/environment variable. Rolling Docker Engine back to 28.x is a temporary workaround.
notes: The daemon rejection reason is not printed in the Testcontainers log; the API-version mismatch is inferred from the engine raising its minimum API version in 29.0.0.
